question: Which Indian state is renowned for the traditional canal irrigation method known as 'Kulh'?
solution:
The correct answer is __Himachal Pradesh__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Kulhs:-

 
 
• 'Kulh' is the most common source of irrigation in the hilly state of Himachal Pradesh.
 
• These​ are small local irrigation canals found in Himachal Pradesh.
 
• They are mainly found in hilly/mountainous regions where they are used to transport melted water from glaciers to villages due to the effect of gravity.
 
• Under this system, water from the streams is diverted into man-made channels that carry this water to various villages.
 
• They serve as a source of canal irrigation for agricultural crops.
 
• Being a hilly area, it was not possible to build tube-wells, borewells in Himachal Pradesh. That's why 'kulhs' came into existence.
 
• They are jointly managed by common neighboring villages.
 
• As of today, most of them are defunct after being taken over by the Irrigation Department.
 
• They are water channels most commonly found in mountain areas.
